deepdive.sec: Fashion & Retail / Textile Sourcing & Experience Centers

bull_bear.body: IPO proceeds allocated to: 1) import of technical textiles (China) and outdoor fabrics (Singapore); 2) store CapEx (Lajpat Nagar, Chandigarh, Dubai); 3) team and tech enhancement; 4) working capital for inventory; 5) increasing bank limit from ₹9.5cr to ₹25cr (in process)
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Working capital cycle at 97 days (up from 68) due to extended credit to exporters affected by US tariffs; reliance on temporary tariff relief (50% → 25% expected in 1-2 months); execution risk in opening 10 experience centers on timeline; dependency on new B2B client (₹100cr order) materializing
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, optimistic, and execution-focused; emphasized profitability over revenue growth; acknowledged temporary working capital strain but framed it as strategic and recoverable; strong belief in 30% revenue and 60% PAT CAGR targets; proactive on scaling via retail and tech
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The 97-day working capital cycle is not a liquidity risk but a calculated margin capture play — they charge higher margins to offset interest cost on extended credit to exporters, turning a supply chain challenge into a pricing advantage
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: B2B fabric: 85% of revenue (targeting 70-75% by 2028); B2C: 13-14% (targeting 20-25%); technical textiles: 2% (targeting 15%); made-to-measure: 1-2%
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Exporters facing 50% US tariffs | TradeUNO | beneficiary | High | TradeUNO turned tariff pain into margin expansion by extending credit to exporters and charging premium, capturing value from disrupted supply chain |
| Traditional textile retailers with low differentiation | Local fabric retailers in Delhi/NCR | loser | Medium | TradeUNO's experience centers with 10k SKUs and international designs threaten low-tech local players |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: Margin expansion driven by: 1) 3-7% cash discounts from suppliers via early payment; 2) shift from low-margin yarn to high-margin B2C/technical textiles; 3) disciplined OpEx control; 4) pricing power via solution-based selling; 5) higher-margin B2B2C model
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: 30% CAGR for FY26 (target: ₹147-150cr); margin: sustained 20%+ EBITDA margin; order inflow: targeting ₹100cr from one large client with 225 stores; capex/commissioning: ₹10-15cr for 10 experience centers over 2.5 years, with first store (Lajpat Nagar) to open by Mar 25
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Expansion into Bangladesh and Dubai; onboarding 150 designers on platform; partnership with 3000cr-revenue retailer for ₹100cr order; Amway-style direct sales channel with women distributors
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: TradeUNO delivered a 60% PAT growth and 790 bps EBITDA margin expansion in H1FY26 through disciplined cost control, supplier cash discounts, and higher-margin B2C/technical textile sales; the company is now scaling via 10 experience centers and large B2B partnerships to drive 30% revenue and 60% PAT CAGR for FY26.
